item.title: Carney warned about economic coercion. Now Trump is testing the Canadian prime minister
item.summary: # Carney warned about economic coercion. Now Trump is testing the Canadian prime minister - Click here to listen to this article - Share via - The renewed trade war ignited by the United States’ latest tariffs turns Canada into a high-stakes test of Prime Minister Carney’s argument about how middle powers confront economic coercion from larger nations. - Carney is doing what many other American allies have so far avoided: risking economic pain rather than yielding to Trump’s tariff pressure. TORONTO — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney drew international attention this year by warning that middle powers must resist economic coercion by more powerful countries. Now, President Trump is putting that warning to the test with sweeping new tariffs that could show how much economic pain Canada can absorb. Tensions escalated late Friday when Canada walked away from negotiations after Carney concluded the United States was demanding too much in exchange for tariff relief. The U.S. imposed 50% duties Saturday on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, and Carney announced dollar-for-dollar retaliation beginning Sept. 8. “We’re going to hit back,” Carney said.
